architecture.mechanism: A localized fault propagates across interconnected subsystem dependencies, converting a single-component failure into a system-wide outage (dependency-driven propagation).
architecture.intervention: Decouple the electronic power steering (EPS) power and communication path from the engine management and steering-lock circuits via separate power domains, an isolation gateway, and a fail-safe limp-home mode with mechanical steering fallback so an EPS fault is contained locally.
architecture.expected_effect: An EPS failure is contained within the steering subsystem, so the engine continues operating and the steering remains controllable even with no prior warning.
architecture.falsification_test: With the engine running and the vehicle in motion, inject a hard short and a loss-of-communication fault into the EPS motor controller, then verify over repeated trials that engine RPM stays within its normal idle band and steering torque remains within manual-assist limits.
